hypothesis: The USB burst loop of the maintenance task moves a framed response in far fewer scheduler ticks than a one-pass-per-tick loop.

conditions.fifo: modeled 2 KiB FIFO, 512-byte endpoint and host turnaround

conclusion: These counts establish scheduling behavior under the model, not physical throughput.
narrative: checks/storage-maintenance-usb-burst.py (removed as a before/after experiment) executed the burst loop and the former one-pass-per-tick loop with the same modeled 2 KiB FIFO, 512-byte endpoint and host turnaround. A 32,840-byte framed response took 8 scheduler ticks rather than 66, and a one-packet response took one rather than two. Idle remained one pass per tick. Delayed or abandoned hosts, counter stalls and failures, expiry, and provider loss or waiting exercised the burst and retention boundaries. The existing DMA and storage-command evidence was reused.
